## Current delivery contract — user-approved two-outcome stack
Owner: PR B. One PR per complete outcome, NOT one PR per bead. Keep detailed beads and cohesive internal commits for tracking; consolidate existing draft foundations into their owning feature PR where practical. PR B stacks on independently usable PR A. Include owning PR documentation and validation there. This supersedes earlier per-bead/prerequisite PR instructions and historical comments. Closed foundation status is not outcome acceptance.
New-feature E2E requires explicit human UX approval in zaq-emb.32; no self-approval.

Deliver one complete outcome PR stacked on PR A: running agents consume authorized durable history without leaks, duplicate context, lost requests or false delivery success. Include Person-bound execution and execution-private state; bounded refresh before internal model calls; fixed request cursors/canonical dedup; between-request context synchronization and cursor advancement; busy/finalizing request handling; ordered intermediary/final delivery and delayed/asynchronous timeout semantics. Distinguish execution persisted, context synchronized and channel delivery confirmed. Test revoked access, exact runtime/request identity, cumulative deltas, tool-call/result pairing, failed/deferred context application, busy admission and delayed timeout. Detailed beads/internal commits are not separate PRs. Include B-specific docs, validation, explicit UX approval before new E2E, coverage/review and final gate. PR A must remain independently usable.

## Alignment update — 2026-10-07 / a0c8796e
First leg .30 is decomposed into zaq-emb.30.1, zaq-emb.30.2, zaq-emb.30.3, zaq-emb.30.4, zaq-emb.30.5. Preserve a0c8796e canonical UUIDs, authorization, conversation-backed execution proof, missing-root readability, query/accounting contracts and tool budgets. .5/.16/.7/.8 and .31 remain required. PR A acceptance separately gates landing; B retains its human UX/E2E/coverage/final gates. Plan-time CI snapshot (10 successful checks, two running browser jobs) is historical, not a current-green claim.
